note: SPEC-18 proposal §4.6: following the change feed with a pull cursor. See vectors/store/README.md §10.

cases.name: nothing-new
cases.note: A pull at the peer's own revision reads no feed and returns nothing.

cases.name: one-append
cases.note: One append after the follow: one record and its one delta.

cases.name: several-records-in-one-page
cases.note: Three commits, one with three deltas that arrive in the reverse of id order. The deltas come ascending by id.

cases.name: pages-of-one
cases.note: The store's pages hold one record. A pull reads one page, so a step takes one pull per record. a-note is added, purged and added again across the pulls of one step.

cases.name: a-head-only-commit
cases.note: A commit that moves only the head: a record with no ids, and no get.

cases.name: a-purge-of-a-held-id
cases.note: a-height leaves the holdings. The record removes it; nothing is delivered.

cases.name: add-then-purge-in-one-page
cases.note: b-name is added and purged after the follow. The page names it twice, and no bytes come: the peer no longer holds it.

cases.name: add-purge-add-in-one-page
cases.note: b-name is added, purged and added again under a new arrival record. It comes once, with its current arrival record.

cases.name: add-purge-add-across-pulls
cases.note: b-name is added and pulled, purged and pulled, added again and pulled. Then purged and added again between two pulls.

cases.name: a-purge-held-by-another-peer-and-a-settled-debt
cases.note: A and B hold b-name. A's purge leaves the bytes with B; B's purge removes them; A's second purge settles a debt and writes no record. Neither follower gets bytes.

cases.name: two-peers
cases.note: A and B commit in turn and share bytes. Each follower reads its own peer's records only.

cases.name: retention-too-short
cases.note: The store keeps one record. Two commits after the follow drop the record the follower needs.

cases.name: a-position-from-the-future
cases.note: The follower stands two revisions past the peer: resync-required, with no feed call.

cases.name: another-peers-history
cases.note: The follower's position carries B's history. Its revision is one of A's, so a feed call could answer; resync-required comes first, with no feed call.

cases.name: pull-after-resync
cases.note: A position one past the peer answers resync-required. Two commits then pass the position. The next pull answers resync-required again, with the first current: the cursor does not ask the store again.

cases.name: a-follower-started-mid-history
cases.note: Four commits, then the follow. Later commits purge an id held before the follow and add it again, and add new ones.
